K.grow.branch grows a forking thing that leans to the light and turns aside from a field it is told about; K.grow.limbs adds it as tubes. K.grow.arrange gives the places of parts in a spiral, a whorl or a rosette (petals, spots, fronds). K.grow.rock is a lump cut by flat faces, laid in beds, with worn edges. K.grow.species wraps a recipe and a set of ranges: every individual draws its own numbers from where it stands. All from a seed; none of it touches the builder's dice.
entries.use: const places = K.grow.scatter(S, { disc: [0, 0, 6], n: 30, shade: [0, 0.4] }); K.grow.species({ vary: { h: [0.3, 0.8] }, make(S, at, v, k) { ... } }).sow(S, places)
entries.keywords: plant tree mushroom rock scatter procedural species

entries.title: Growth that runs in steps: settle, creep, spread
entries.summary: K.grow.settle drops a shape until it touches what is there and leans it to the ground (K.grow.rock with settle: true). K.grow.creep walks a creeper over the surface toward a direction, forking now and then; K.grow.vine gives it a stem and swept leaves. K.grow.spread grows a patch over the surface step by step where a rule allows it, and gives a mask for S.cover (lichen, moss, frost, rust). Also K.grow.scatterIn (points inside a shape) and K.grow.ray (where a line meets the scene).
entries.use: K.grow.creep(S, { from, dir: [0, 1, 0], steps: 40 }) ; K.grow.spread(S, { from: [p], ok: (x, y, z, n) => n[1] > 0.3 })
entries.keywords: settle creeper vine lichen spread simulation

entries.title: A mesh from a file becomes a solid
entries.summary: OBJ (with MTL), glTF and GLB are read, fitted to the scene, and turned into a signed-distance field on a grid: exact distance near the faces, swept outward; inside or outside by counting crossings along three axes. From there it joins, is carved, breaks and bakes like any other solid. Colours come from materials and vertex colours and become palette ramps; textures are not read. An open mesh is treated as a sheet with thickness.

entries.use:
mesh-topology inspect|triangulate <mesh.json> [--out file.json]   inspect authored connectivity or derive triangles

mesh-topology select <mesh-or-scene.json> <query.json> [--object id] [--from selection.json] [--view settings.json | --visibility capture.json] [--out file.json]   select authored components
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> [--origin X,Y,Z] [--right X,Y,Z] [--up X,Y,Z] [--grid N|U,V] [--from-camera] [--yaw R] [--pitch R] [--at seconds] [--camera-shot ID] [--lock x|y|z|off] [--out file.json]   set or camera-pick the shared construction plane
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> [--grid N|U,V | --grid-preset texel|brick|module] [--grid-tileset ID] [--module-size N|U,V] [--rounding nearest|floor|ceiling] [--out file.json]   set construction grid increments and snapping mode
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> --edge-object ID --edge ID --tilt DEGREES [--edge-from VERTEX] [--edge-at T] [--reference-up X,Y,Z] [--grid N|U,V] [--out file.json]   hinge the working plane on an authored edge
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> (--tilt DEGREES | --detach-edge) [--out file.json]   adjust or detach the retained edge anchor
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> --snap-origin vertex --object ID --vertex ID [--detach-edge] [--out file.json]   snap the working origin to a scene vertex
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> --snap-origin instance --instance ID [--instance-kind prefab|asset-part] [--detach-edge] [--out file.json]   snap the working origin to an instance frame
mesh-topology plane <scene.json> --snap-origin bounds|average --object ID --selection selection.json [--detach-edge] [--out file.json]   snap the working origin to a selected center
mesh-topology move <mesh-or-scene.json> [--object id] [--part id] --vertex id --by X,Y,Z [--space local|world|plane|camera] [--view file] [--align plane|grid] [--coincident [--coincident-distance N]] [--expect revision] [--out file.json]   move a vertex and optionally its coincident copies
mesh-topology pivot <mesh-or-scene.json> [request.json] [--object id] [--part id] [--selection file] [--out file.json]   place an independent transform pivot
mesh-topology transform <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--selection file] [--view file | --pivot file] [--out file] [--report file]   transform, mirror, snap, push or randomize mesh components
mesh-topology transform <mesh-or-scene.json> <random-receipt.json> --replay [--object id] [--out file] [--report file]   replay recorded positions on the source revision
mesh-topology health <mesh-or-scene.json> [settings.json] [--object id] [--out report.json]   locate local topology and geometry problems
mesh-topology overlaps <mesh-or-scene.json> [settings.json] [--object id] [--part id] [--out report.json | --selection-out faces.json]   review same-facing coincident polygons
mesh-topology isolate-prefab <scene.json> <request.json> [--preview image.png] [--view settings.json] [--out scene.json]   limit prefab instance edits to active faces
mesh-topology repair <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--out file] [--report file]   preview or apply weld, dissolve, winding and quad diagonal edits
mesh-topology cut <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--out file] [--report file] [--pieces dir]   preview or apply plane and knife cuts
mesh-topology face-region <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--out file] [--report file]   preview or apply face extrusion, inset and thickening
mesh-topology edge-edit <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--out file] [--report file]   preview or apply loop insertion, edge slides, bridges and grid fills
mesh-topology retopology <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--surface file] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   snap guided quad patches and stitch an authored rim
mesh-topology boolean <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--operand mesh.json] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   solve and compare mesh or SDF Booleans
mesh-topology bevel <mesh-or-scene.json> <request.json> [--object id] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   preview or apply an edge bevel with native-grid protection
mesh-topology shading <mesh-or-scene.json> [request.json] [--object id] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--subdivision level] [--out file] [--report file]   inspect or edit corner normals, smooth edges and subdivision creases
mesh-topology shape-keys <mesh-or-scene.json> [request.json] [--object id] [--view file --preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   edit the rest model or capture a named pose correction
mesh-topology skin <mesh-or-scene.json> [request.json] [--object id] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   inspect, paint, mirror and preview named joint weights
mesh-topology modifiers inspect|set|update|apply <mesh-or-scene.json> [stack-or-edit.json] [--object id] [--through id] [--targets file] [--diagnostics] [--view file] [--preview dir] [--out file] [--report file]   inspect or edit a retained mesh modifier stack
mesh-topology correspond <before.json> <after.json> [--lineage links.json] [--projection settings.json] [--match-ids on|off] [--out map.json]   map stable and projected elements

entries.title: Bounce light, baked
entries.summary: Optional (S.bounce = { k, reach, rays, glow, tint }, or --bounce on the command line; B.bounce(S.sdf, o) by hand). After a bake every plain dab sends a few lines out over the side it faces; where one lands, the colour already there is what arrives, weaker with distance, more from things that glow. The dab moves up its own ramp by that much, and takes another palette colour only where what arrives is strongly coloured. Shadows beside bright things fill in. It is subtle at k 1 (two or three pixels in a hundred change) and costs three to four times the bake. Only palette colours are used.

entries.title: A lamp that stays put: shadows, its own colours, flicker
entries.summary: On top of the moving lamps of K.light.system. K.light.shadow(st, cap, lamp, S.sdf) works out once what the lamp can see, so it casts shadows and can then be dimmed, switched off and on and recoloured for nothing. lamp.ramp = [dark .. bright] paints what it mostly lights from its own colours (a fire's orange on stone). K.light.flicker(sys, lamp, { rate, depth }) makes it gutter. To have a baked lamp flicker, leave it out of S.lights and give it to K.light.system this way.
entries.use: const lit = st.add(K.light.system(st, cap, [lamp])); K.light.shadow(st, cap, lamp, S.sdf); st.add(K.light.flicker(lit, lamp))

entries.title: Fur
entries.summary: Each point of skin grows a few hairs of three strokes that droop more toward the tip, so a hair curves. The coat lies along a comb direction laid into the surface; neighbouring hairs lean and lengthen together (a slow noise), which makes locks. Root darker, tip lighter; where the light rakes across the coat the tips step up again (sheen), and round the edge of the lit side they catch the light from behind (rim, with its own ramp). The skin under it is two tones down.

entries.title: Glass that bends what is behind it
entries.summary: Faint tinted splats marked as glass. Their coverage is kept in a spare channel of the depth picture; the final pass looks the picture up a little to one side by how that coverage changes, so the bend is strongest at the rim of a jar and nothing in the flat of a pane. Make the solid a ghost so it shades and hides nothing.
entries.use: S.lathe(c, h, profile, K.look.glass([6, 7, 8], { a: 0.085 }), { ghost: true })   ·   K.glint(B, p, axis, len, col)   ·   B.finish({ refract: 7 })

entries.title: Inked detail: colour looked up for each pixel
entries.summary: Optional, off unless asked for. A plain dab is one flat colour, so a line thinner than a dab comes out ragged. With S.fine = 1 (or --fine on the command line) each plain dab is also baked with a 4 by 4 picture of the surface under it: its pattern, the edge of a cast shadow, something cut into it, a flush neighbour. Compatible host renderers and the headless renderer look the colour up for each pixel from where on the dab that pixel is. Thin cuts (runes, comb cells, seams) come out whole; broad surfaces do not change. Costs: baking takes four to five times as long, twelve more numbers a dab. A dab recoloured after baking is drawn plain. Not followed by parts moved by K.rig on the CPU (bones on the graphics card are).

entries.title: Light through a body: wax and jelly
entries.summary: At the bake each point measures how far it is through the solid toward the sun and how far straight in. Light that has come a short way through arrives on the side turned away from the sun and dies off smoothly with distance, so thin parts are bright, thick ones show a dark saturated band, and the lit side wraps softly round the terminator. A glow ramp (dark to bright) takes over where the light comes through. A light inside the body (core) shows through the skin as the eye at S.view sees it; gloss adds a small wet highlight where the body mirrors the sun to the eye. Best lit from behind. True see-through (a under 1) dithers in a palette, so it is kept for thin things like glass.

entries.title: One solver for jelly, clay, sand and water
entries.summary: The material point method: splats are the points, a coarse grid carries forces between them. Jelly springs back, clay gives and stays, sand has friction and no pull, water keeps only its volume. Splats of stuff that keeps a shape are stretched and turned with it. Fixed step, so the same at any frame rate; goes to sleep at rest. Static solids and moving colliders push it; a tap shoves it or scoops a bite out.

entries.title: A shape typed in, a block at a time
entries.summary: A model is a pile of small pictures made of letters; every letter is a material and '.' is nothing. It is not drawn as blocks: by default the blocks only say where the stuff is, and what is made of them is one soft solid (faces stay where they were typed, corners and steps are rounded, a hole one block deep is a dimple), with each letter's material where it was typed. hard: true keeps flat faces and square corners. Either way it is a solid like any other: it lights, shadows, joins a group, carves with neg, rides a bone with tag.

entries.title: More ways to join and repeat solids
entries.summary: K.sculpt(S) adds S.join(kind, a, b, {r, n}) with kinds union, cut, common, round, chamfer, stairs, columns (and cut/common versions), pipe, engrave, groove, tongue; S.fold(p, {polar | mirror | repeat}); S.poly and S.regular('d4'..'d20') with a frame on every face. Operands are solids made with { hold: true }. Also: S.warp(p, { twist | bend | taper | map }) sees a held solid through bent space; S.shell (hollow skin), S.swell (grown all round), S.rough (surface pushed by a function); S.extrude and S.revolve make flat outlines solid, with K.poly2.ngon/star/gear/rect/svg/with for the outlines (an SVG path can be extruded). Not added: elongate, and the oddities (blob, the baroque picture frame). S.inflate is S.swell under its usual name; S.bubbles(p, { cell, h, flat }) raises a surface into rows of domes (bubble wrap); S.puff(outline, c, height) blows a flat outline up like a cushion or a balloon letter.

entries.title: Ghost pictures and taps from the command line
entries.summary: ink-studio ghost draws one moment with those either side laid faintly over it, so what moved and how far shows at a glance. --poke 2:x,y,z taps a diorama at a time, toward a point, in any command that plays it, so reactions can be drawn and checked without a browser.

entries.title: Mist, shafts of light, distance haze
entries.summary: K.mist lays a low drifting haze of soft splats; K.shafts puts beams in the air; fog in B.finish fades things toward a palette colour with distance. All three cost nothing per frame in JS.
entries.use: K.mist(B, { rad, y, depth, n, cols, a, where })   ·   K.shafts(B, { from, dir, len, r, col })   ·   B.finish({ fog: { c: 29, start: 0.62, max: 0.38 } })
entries.keywords: fog mist haze god rays shafts

entries.title: Smoke that shades itself
entries.summary: Soft puffs carried by a current. Each frame every puff looks toward the light and adds up the smoke in its way (a coarse grid), and that decides its colour: bright on the lit side, dark inside and underneath.
entries.use: const smoke = st.add(K.smoke(st, pool, { at, ramp: [lit ... dark], sun, rate, life, size, rise, flow })); smoke.burst(p, 10)
